s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

differentials: hypokalemic periodic paralysis due to scn4a mutation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness, urinary retention, and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, combined with the MRI findings of nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, are most consistent with spinal cord compression.

rejected.label: quadriparesis
rejected.why: While the patient has quadriparesis, it is a symptom rather than a diagnosis.

rejected.label: neuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more suggestive of a compressive lesion rather than a primary neuropathy.

rejected.label: urinary retention
rejected.why: Urinary retention is a symptom that can be caused by spinal cord compression, but it is not a diagnosis in itself.

rejected.label: ptosis
rejected.why: Ptosis is a symptom that can be caused by various conditions, but it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's overall clinical presentation.
